# Tool reference

[Documentation home](../../README.md) · [Workflows and pagination](../usage.md) · [Authentication](../authentication.md)

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-tool-docs.mjs. Do not edit directly. -->

The registry exposes **69 tools**; **10** declare output schemas. Regenerate with `npm run docs:generate`. CI checks this file for drift.

Parameters, defaults, constraints, and descriptions below come from the registry used by MCP discovery. Runtime refinements and GitLab permissions can impose additional constraints. A default makes a parameter optional; “required” describes the input before defaults are applied.

Every tool accepts optional `userCredentials` with `accessToken` and optional `gitlabUrl`. A null/empty credential object falls back to transport/environment credentials. Host overrides are ignored with host pinning enabled. See [credential precedence](../authentication.md#credential-precedence); prefer transport secrets over tokens in tool arguments.

“Write” uses the registry classification. `execute_custom_query` is dynamic: parsed mutations require write authority. Custom GraphQL/REST tools require user credentials unless shared escape-hatch access is explicitly enabled. Annotations and read classifications are not authorization grants.

All results contain JSON text; objects also include structured content. Declared output schemas are shown where present. Additional instance-specific fields may be preserved. See [result contracts](../usage.md#result-contracts-and-errors) for errors, arrays, and null results.

## analytics_group_summary

Aggregated activity summary for an entire group (optionally including subgroups) over a time window — totals by action type (pushes, MRs opened/merged, comments, approvals), with breakdowns by project, by contributor, and by day. Use this to answer "what did this team do" without fanning out across list_project_events yourself.

Access: **Read**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `group` | string | Yes | min length 1 | Group full path (e.g. "my-group" or "my-group/sub-group") |
| `since` | string | Yes | — | ISO date/datetime, inclusive lower bound (e.g. "2026-04-01" or "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z") |
| `until` | string | No | — | ISO date/datetime, inclusive upper bound. Defaults to now. |
| `includeSubgroups` | boolean | No | default true | Recurse into subgroup projects. Defaults to true. |
| `topContributors` | integer | No | min 1; max 100; default 10 | Cap on the byUser[] list (sorted by event count desc). Default 10. |
| `maxEvents` | integer | No | min 1; max 10000 | Global cap on events fetched across all projects. Defaults to 2000; envelope flags truncated:true if reached. |
| `maxProjects` | integer | No | min 1; max 2000 | Cap on projects scanned. Defaults to 500. |

## analytics_review_bottlenecks

Aggregate open (non-draft) merge requests across a group or project to surface review bottlenecks. Returns per-reviewer queue stats, age-bucket histogram, and the stalest MRs by updatedAt. MRs with no reviewer assigned are bucketed under "(unassigned)".

Access: **Read**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `group` | string | No | — | Group full path (e.g. "my-group"). Mutually exclusive with `project`. |
| `project` | string | No | — | Project full path (e.g. "my-group/my-project"). Mutually exclusive with `group`. |
| `staleAfterDays` | integer | No | min 0; max 9007199254740991; default 3 | An MR counts as "stale" if its updatedAt is older than this many days. Default 3. |
| `topStalest` | integer | No | min 1; max 200; default 20 | Cap on the stalest[] list. Default 20. |
| `maxMRs` | integer | No | min 1; max 5000; default 1000 | Hard cap on MRs scanned. Envelope flags `truncated:true` if reached. |

## analytics_user_summary

Aggregated activity summary for a user over a time window — totals by action type (pushes, MRs opened/merged, comments, approvals), breakdown by project and by day. Use this instead of list_user_events when you want counts rather than a raw event feed.

Access: **Read**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `user` | string | Yes | min length 1 | Username (e.g. "alice") or numeric user ID |
| `since` | string | Yes | — | ISO date/datetime, inclusive lower bound (e.g. "2026-03-01" or "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z") |
| `until` | string | No | — | ISO date/datetime, inclusive upper bound. Defaults to now. |
| `maxEvents` | integer | No | min 1; max 5000 | Cap on events fetched. Defaults to 2000; returned envelope has truncated:true if reached. |

## award_achievement

Award an achievement to a GitLab username. Multiple awards to the same user are allowed. Requires group Maintainer/Owner. GitLab notifies the recipient, who may need to accept before it appears on their profile.

Access: **Write**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `achievementId` | string | Yes | min length 1 | Numeric achievement ID or gid://gitlab/Achievements::Achievement/&lt;id&gt;. |
| `username` | string | Yes | min length 1 | — |
| `awardMessage` | string | No | — | Optional award message, supported on instances exposing this mutation field. |

## create_achievement

Create a group achievement with name and optional description. Requires group Maintainer/Owner and enabled Achievements. Set avatars in GitLab UI; file uploads are not supported by this tool.

Access: **Write**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `group` | string | Yes | min length 1 | Group full path, for example my-group/sub-group. |
| `name` | string | Yes | min length 1 | — |
| `description` | string | No | — | — |

## create_broadcast_message

Create a GitLab broadcast message. Requires administrator privileges on the GitLab instance.

Access: **Write**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | string | Yes | min length 1 | Message text to display |
| `starts_at` | string | No | format date-time; pattern ^(?:(?:\d\d[2468][048]&#124;\d\d[13579][26]&#124;\d\d0[48]&#124;[02468][048]00&#124;[13579][26]00)-02-29&#124;\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]&#124;1[02])-(?:0[1-9]&#124;[12]\d&#124;3[01])&#124;(?:0[469]&#124;11)-(?:0[1-9]&#124;[12]\d&#124;30)&#124;(?:02)-(?:0[1-9]&#124;1\d&#124;2[0-8])))T(?:(?:[01]\d&#124;2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d(?:\.\d+)?(?:Z))$ | ISO 8601 timestamp when the message starts |
| `ends_at` | string | No | format date-time; pattern ^(?:(?:\d\d[2468][048]&#124;\d\d[13579][26]&#124;\d\d0[48]&#124;[02468][048]00&#124;[13579][26]00)-02-29&#124;\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]&#124;1[02])-(?:0[1-9]&#124;[12]\d&#124;3[01])&#124;(?:0[469]&#124;11)-(?:0[1-9]&#124;[12]\d&#124;30)&#124;(?:02)-(?:0[1-9]&#124;1\d&#124;2[0-8])))T(?:(?:[01]\d&#124;2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d(?:\.\d+)?(?:Z))$ | ISO 8601 timestamp when the message ends |
| `color` | string | No | — | Background color in hex format, e.g. "#E75E40" |
| `font` | string | No | — | Foreground (font) color in hex format |
| `target_access_levels` | array of integer | No | — | Access levels to target: 10=Guest, 20=Reporter, 30=Developer, 40=Maintainer, 50=Owner |
| `target_path` | string | No | — | Path glob for pages where the message should appear |
| `broadcast_type` | "banner", "notification" | No | — | Broadcast type: "banner" or "notification" |
| `dismissable` | boolean | No | — | Whether users can dismiss the broadcast message |
| `theme` | string | No | — | Theme name (GitLab 16.9+), e.g. "indigo", "red" |

## execute_custom_query

Execute custom GraphQL queries for complex filtering (e.g., issues with assigneeUsernames: ["user"], labelName: ["bug"]). Use this for structured filtering by assignee/author/labels when search tools return 0 results. Use pagination and limit complexity to avoid timeouts.

Access: **Dynamic (query or mutation)**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string | Yes | — | GraphQL query string. Example: query { issues(assigneeUsernames: ["cdhanlon"], state: opened, first: 50) { nodes { iid title webUrl } } } |
| `variables` | object | No | — | Variables for the GraphQL query |
| `requiresWrite` | boolean | No | default false | Hint that this needs write access. Mutations are auto-detected and always write-gated regardless of this flag. |

<details>
<summary>Nested parameter schemas</summary>

```json
{
  "variables": {
    "description": "Variables for the GraphQL query",
    "type": "object",
    "propertyNames": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "additionalProperties": {}
  }
}
```

</details>

## execute_rest_read

Execute an arbitrary GET request against the GitLab REST API at /api/v4. Open-ended escape hatch for read endpoints not covered by a dedicated tool — e.g. /projects/:id/repository/files, /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/test_report, /admin/*. Provide the path beginning with "/" (no host, no /api/v4 prefix) and an optional query object. For writes, use execute_rest_write.

Access: **Read**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | Yes | min length 1 | Path under /api/v4, beginning with "/" (e.g. "/projects/42/issues" or "/projects/foo%2Fbar/repository/commits/HEAD"). Must not include host, "/api/v4" prefix, or "?" query string. |
| `query` | object | No | — | Query string parameters (e.g. { state: "opened", per_page: 20 }). Values are coerced to strings. |

<details>
<summary>Nested parameter schemas</summary>

```json
{
  "query": {
    "description": "Query string parameters (e.g. { state: \"opened\", per_page: 20 }). Values are coerced to strings.",
    "type": "object",
    "propertyNames": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "additionalProperties": {
      "type": [
        "string",
        "number",
        "boolean"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

## execute_rest_write

Execute an arbitrary POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE request against the GitLab REST API at /api/v4. Open-ended escape hatch for write endpoints not covered by a dedicated tool. Destructive — DELETE is permitted, so check the path before invoking. For reads, use execute_rest_read.

Access: **Write**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE" | Yes | — | HTTP method. DELETE is destructive and not reversible. |
| `path` | string | Yes | min length 1 | Path under /api/v4, beginning with "/" (e.g. "/projects/42/issues" or "/projects/foo%2Fbar/merge_requests/3/merge"). Must not include host, "/api/v4" prefix, or "?" query string. |
| `body` | object or array of any JSON value or string or number or boolean or null | No | — | Request body as a JSON value or JSON-encoded string. Sent as application/json; nested objects are preserved. Omit for endpoints that don't take a body (most DELETE / some PUT). |
| `query` | object | No | — | Query string parameters. Most write endpoints take their args in the body, but a few mix. |

<details>
<summary>Nested parameter schemas</summary>

```json
{
  "query": {
    "description": "Query string parameters. Most write endpoints take their args in the body, but a few mix.",
    "type": "object",
    "propertyNames": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "additionalProperties": {
      "type": [
        "string",
        "number",
        "boolean"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

## get_group_projects

List projects inside a GitLab group (optionally filter by search term)

Access: **Read**.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## get_issue_context

Bundle issue body, all notes (paginated up to maxNotes), related merge requests (mentioning), closing merge requests, linked issues (relates_to/blocks/is_blocked_by) into a single call. Use this instead of fanning out across get_issues + get_notes + search_merge_requests when investigating an issue.

Access: **Read**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectPath` | string | Yes | min length 1 | Full project path (e.g. "my-group/my-project") |
| `iid` | string | Yes | min length 1 | Issue IID (the number shown in the GitLab UI) |
| `maxNotes` | integer | No | min 1; max 500; default 100 | Cap on notes fetched. Default 100. |
| `includeSystemNotes` | boolean | No | default false | Include system-generated notes (label changes, assignment events). Default false. |

## get_issues

Get issues from a specific GitLab project (read-only)

Access: **Read**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectPath` | string | Yes | — | Full path of the project (e.g., "group/project-name") |
| `first` | number | No | min 1; max 100; default 20 | Number of issues to retrieve |
| `after` | string | No | — | Pagination cursor. To fetch the next page, pass the previous response pageInfo.endCursor here and repeat until pageInfo.hasNextPage is false. Paginating this way is the reliable path to complete results and accurate totals. |
| `sort` | string | No | — | Sort order (e.g., UPDATED_DESC, CREATED_DESC, CREATED_ASC). Defaults to UPDATED_DESC for recency. |
| `fetchAll` | boolean | No | default false | Fetch multiple pages in one call, up to "first" items total (max 100) — NOT exhaustive. For complete results or accurate counts, leave this false and paginate via after (pageInfo.endCursor). |

<details>
<summary>Declared output schema</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "nodes": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
```

| `after` | string | No | — | Only events after this date (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `sort` | "asc", "desc" | No | default "desc" | Sort order (default desc — newest first) |
| `page` | integer | No | min 1; max 9007199254740991; default 1 | Page number (1-based) |
| `per_page` | integer | No | min 1; max 100; default 20 | Results per page |

## list_work_items

List work items within a namespace (group or project fullPath). Supports filtering by type (ISSUE, TASK, EPIC, INCIDENT, OBJECTIVE, KEY_RESULT) and state, plus cursor pagination and fetchAll.

Access: **Read**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fullPath` | string | Yes | — | Namespace full path — group (e.g. "my-group") or project (e.g. "my-group/my-project") |
| `types` | array of "ISSUE", "TASK", "EPIC", "INCIDENT", "OBJECTIVE", "KEY_RESULT", "TEST_CASE", "REQUIREMENT" | No | — | Filter by work item types. Omit for all types. |
| `state` | "opened", "closed", "all" | No | — | Filter by state. "all" returns every state. |
| `first` | integer | No | min 1; max 100; default 20 | Page size (default 20, capped by server maxPageSize) |
| `after` | string | No | — | Cursor for next page |
| `fetchAll` | boolean | No | — | Auto-paginate up to first items |
| `sort` | string | No | — | Sort enum, e.g. UPDATED_DESC (default), CREATED_DESC, TITLE_ASC |

## manage_pipeline

Retry or cancel a CI/CD pipeline (requires user authentication with write permissions)

Access: **Write**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectPath` | string | Yes | — | Full path of the project (e.g., "group/project-name") |
| `pipelineIid` | string | Yes | — | Pipeline IID |
| `action` | "retry", "cancel" | Yes | — | Action to perform on the pipeline |

## mark_all_todos_done

Mark pending to-do items as done for the authenticated user. With no arguments, marks every pending todo. Optional scoping args (groupPath, projectPath, action, type, authorIds, targetId) narrow which todos are marked. Irreversible without per-item restore_todo calls. Returns the actual list of updated todos.

Access: **Write**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `groupPath` | string | No | — | Limit to a group by full path. Resolved to a node GID server-side. |
| `projectPath` | string | No | — | Limit to a project by full path. Resolved to a node GID server-side. |
| `action` | string | No | — | Limit to todos with this action (e.g. assigned, mentioned, review_requested). |
| `type` | string | No | — | Limit to todos targeting this type (e.g. Issue, MergeRequest, Epic). |
| `authorIds` | array of string | No | — | Limit to todos authored by these users. Numeric IDs or gid://gitlab/User/N strings. |
| `targetId` | string | No | — | Limit to todos for a single target (e.g. a specific issue/MR GID). |

## mark_todo_done

Mark a single to-do item as done for the authenticated user. Requires the todo's ID (numeric or full gid://gitlab/Todo/N form) from list_my_todos.

Access: **Write**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `todoId` | string | Yes | min length 1 | Todo ID — accepts a bare numeric ID ("42") or a full gid ("gid://gitlab/Todo/42") |

## resolve_path

Resolve a GitLab path to either a project or group and list group projects when applicable

Access: **Read**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fullPath` | string | Yes | min length 1 | Project or group full path (e.g., "group/subgroup/project") |
| `first` | number | No | min 1; max 100; default 20 | Number of items to retrieve when listing group projects |
| `after` | string | No | — | Pagination cursor. To fetch the next page, pass the previous response pageInfo.endCursor here and repeat until pageInfo.hasNextPage is false. Paginating this way is the reliable path to complete results and accurate totals. |

## restore_todo

Restore a previously-marked-done to-do item back to pending state. Accepts the todo's ID (numeric or full gid://gitlab/Todo/N form).

Access: **Write**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `todoId` | string | Yes | min length 1 | Todo ID — accepts a bare numeric ID ("42") or a full gid ("gid://gitlab/Todo/42") |

## revoke_achievement

Revoke one awarded achievement. Provide either userAchievementId, or group + achievementId + username. Username lookup scans recipient pages and rejects ambiguous repeated awards; use a specific userAchievementId in that case. Requires group Maintainer/Owner.

Access: **Write**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `userAchievementId` | string | No | min length 1 | Numeric award ID or gid://gitlab/Achievements::UserAchievement/&lt;id&gt;. This identifies one award, not the achievement definition. |
| `group` | string | No | min length 1 | Group full path, for example my-group/sub-group. |
| `achievementId` | string | No | min length 1 | Numeric achievement ID or gid://gitlab/Achievements::Achievement/&lt;id&gt;. |
| `username` | string | No | min length 1 | — |

## search_gitlab

Text search across GitLab projects and issues (Note: Does not support filtering by assignee/labels - use search_issues for that. MRs cannot be searched globally - use search_merge_requests with username)

Access: **Read**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `searchTerm` | string | No | — | Search term (leave empty for recent activity) |
| `first` | number | No | min 1; max 100; default 20 | Number of results to retrieve per category |
| `after` | string | No | — | Pagination cursor. To fetch the next page, pass the previous response pageInfo.endCursor here and repeat until pageInfo.hasNextPage is false. Paginating this way is the reliable path to complete results and accurate totals. |
| `fetchAll` | boolean | No | default false | Fetch multiple pages per category up to first items each (default 20, max 100), starting at after — NOT exhaustive. Each category returns its own pageInfo. Use search_projects and search_issues to continue those categories independently. |

## search_groups

Search for GitLab groups and organizations

Access: **Read**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `searchTerm` | string | Yes | — | Search term to find groups by name or path |
| `first` | number | No | min 1; max 100; default 20 | Number of groups to retrieve |
| `after` | string | No | — | Pagination cursor. To fetch the next page, pass the previous response pageInfo.endCursor here and repeat until pageInfo.hasNextPage is false. Paginating this way is the reliable path to complete results and accurate totals. |
| `fetchAll` | boolean | No | default false | Fetch multiple pages in one call, up to "first" items total (max 100) — NOT exhaustive. For complete results or accurate counts, leave this false and paginate via after (pageInfo.endCursor). |

## search_issues

Search for issues with text search and/or structured filtering (assignee, author, labels, state). For filtering by assignee/author/labels without text search, leave searchTerm empty.

Access: **Read**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `searchTerm` | string | No | — | Text search term (optional - leave empty to filter by assignee/author/labels only) |
| `projectPath` | string | No | — | Optional project path (e.g., "group/project"). Omit for global search. |
| `state` | string | No | default "all" | Filter by issue state (opened, closed, all) |
| `assigneeUsernames` | array of string | No | — | Filter by assignee usernames (e.g., ["cdhanlon", "jsmith"]) |
| `authorUsername` | string | No | — | Filter by author username (e.g., "cdhanlon") |
| `labelNames` | array of string | No | — | Filter by label names (e.g., ["Priority::High", "bug"]) |
| `first` | number | No | min 1; max 100; default 20 | Number of issues to retrieve |
| `after` | string | No | — | Pagination cursor. To fetch the next page, pass the previous response pageInfo.endCursor here and repeat until pageInfo.hasNextPage is false. Paginating this way is the reliable path to complete results and accurate totals. |
| `sort` | string | No | — | Sort order (e.g., UPDATED_DESC, CREATED_DESC, CREATED_ASC). Defaults to UPDATED_DESC for recency. |
| `fetchAll` | boolean | No | default false | Fetch multiple pages in one call, up to "first" items total (max 100) — NOT exhaustive. For complete results or accurate counts, leave this false and paginate via after (pageInfo.endCursor). |

## search_notes

Full-text search across issue and merge request comments. Scope can be global, a project, or a group. NOTE: on self-hosted GitLab, the "notes" search scope requires Advanced Search (Elasticsearch) to be enabled — without it, this endpoint returns an error. search_gitlab does NOT search note bodies; this tool does.

Access: **Read**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | string | Yes | min length 1 | Search term. Trimmed; empty rejected. |
| `scope` | "global", "project", "group" | No | default "global" | Search scope. Default global. |
| `projectPath` | string | No | — | Required when scope=project. Full project path. |
| `groupPath` | string | No | — | Required when scope=group. Full group path. |
| `perPage` | integer | No | min 1; max 100; default 20 | Results per page. Default 20. |
| `page` | integer | No | min 1; max 9007199254740991; default 1 | Page number. Default 1. |

## update_broadcast_message

Update an existing GitLab broadcast message. Requires administrator privileges.

Access: **Write**.

| Parameter | Type / allowed values | Required | Constraints / default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | Yes | min -9007199254740991; max 9007199254740991 | Broadcast message ID |
| `message` | string | No | min length 1 | Message text to display |
| `starts_at` | string | No | format date-time; pattern ^(?:(?:\d\d[2468][048]&#124;\d\d[13579][26]&#124;\d\d0[48]&#124;[02468][048]00&#124;[13579][26]00)-02-29&#124;\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]&#124;1[02])-(?:0[1-9]&#124;[12]\d&#124;3[01])&#124;(?:0[469]&#124;11)-(?:0[1-9]&#124;[12]\d&#124;30)&#124;(?:02)-(?:0[1-9]&#124;1\d&#124;2[0-8])))T(?:(?:[01]\d&#124;2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d(?:\.\d+)?(?:Z))$ | ISO 8601 timestamp when the message starts |
| `ends_at` | string | No | format date-time; pattern ^(?:(?:\d\d[2468][048]&#124;\d\d[13579][26]&#124;\d\d0[48]&#124;[02468][048]00&#124;[13579][26]00)-02-29&#124;\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]&#124;1[02])-(?:0[1-9]&#124;[12]\d&#124;3[01])&#124;(?:0[469]&#124;11)-(?:0[1-9]&#124;[12]\d&#124;30)&#124;(?:02)-(?:0[1-9]&#124;1\d&#124;2[0-8])))T(?:(?:[01]\d&#124;2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d(?:\.\d+)?(?:Z))$ | ISO 8601 timestamp when the message ends |
| `color` | string | No | — | Background color in hex format, e.g. "#E75E40" |
| `font` | string | No | — | Foreground (font) color in hex format |
| `target_access_levels` | array of integer | No | — | Access levels to target: 10=Guest, 20=Reporter, 30=Developer, 40=Maintainer, 50=Owner |
| `target_path` | string | No | — | Path glob for pages where the message should appear |
| `broadcast_type` | "banner", "notification" | No | — | Broadcast type: "banner" or "notification" |
| `dismissable` | boolean | No | — | Whether users can dismiss the broadcast message |
| `theme` | string | No | — | Theme name (GitLab 16.9+), e.g. "indigo", "red" |
